title: Linking actions and helper verbs
description: Chain actions together ('go and come', 'eat and see'), say 'have done', and use the helper verbs that give Kannada its flavour.

guide.title: The 'having done' form
guide.text:
Kannada does not join verbs with 'and'. Instead, every verb except the last is put in a short form meaning 'having done' (the verbal participle), and only the final verb carries tense and person: oota maadi banni, 'having-done meal, come' = 'eat and then come'.

How to form it:
Regular verbs in -u change -u to -i: maadu - ಮಾಡಿ (maadi); hogu - ಹೋಗಿ (hogi); nodu - ನೋಡಿ (nodi); kelu - ಕೇಳಿ (keli); helu - ಹೇಳಿ (heli); aagu - ಆಗಿ (aagi). (This looks the same as the polite command; the position in the sentence tells you which it is.)

Verbs with an irregular past use the past stem + u: baa - ಬಂದು (bandu); tinnu - ತಿಂದು (tindu); kudi - ಕುಡಿದು (kudidu); kodu - ಕೊಟ್ಟು (kottu); iru - ಇದ್ದು (iddu); tago - ತಗೊಂಡು (tagondu); kootko - ಕೂತ್ಕೊಂಡು (kootkondu); nillu - ನಿಂತು (nintu); elu - ಎದ್ದು (eddu); bare - ಬರೆದು (baredu); mare - ಮರೆತು (maretu).

Several can be chained: angadige hogi, haalu tagondu, bega baa - 'go to the shop, get milk and come back quickly'.

examples.english: I'll go to the shop and come back.
Bring some milk. (take milk and come)

guide.title: 'Have done': participle + iru
guide.text:
Add the present of iru to the participle and you get the perfect, 'have done': maadi + iddeeni = ಮಾಡಿದ್ದೀನಿ (maadiddeeni), 'I have done'.

maadiddeeni, maadiddeeya, maadiddaane, maadiddaale, maadide, maadiddeevi, maadiddeera, maadiddaare.

With irregular verbs: bandiddeeni (I have come), hogiddaare (they have gone), tindiddeeni (I have eaten), kottiddeeni (I have given), nodiddeeni (I have seen), bandide (it has come).

Careful with the look-alikes: maadide can be 'I did' (past) or 'it has done' (perfect neuter). Context decides.

Negative: participle + illa: ಬಂದಿಲ್ಲ (bandilla) hasn't come; ಮಾಡಿಲ್ಲ (maadilla) haven't done; ನೋಡಿಲ್ಲ (nodilla) haven't seen. Same for all persons.

With the past of iru you get 'had done': bandidde, 'I had come'.

Written forms: maadiddene, bandiddaare, bandide.

examples.english: They have gone to their home town.

guide.title: Helper verbs after the participle
guide.text:
A participle followed by certain common verbs gives shades of meaning that English expresses with adverbs or not at all. The helper loses its own meaning.

ಬಿಡು (bidu, 'leave') - completely, once and for all, get it over with: maadibidi, 'get it done'; hogibidi, 'just go'; maretubitte, 'I clean forgot'; tindubitta, 'he ate it all up'.

ಕೊಳ್ಳು (kollu, spoken ko, 'take') - do it for oneself: tagolli, 'take (for yourself)'; kootkolli, 'sit yourself down'; nodkolli, 'look after it / see for yourself'; its 'I' form is -kolteeni: nodkolteeni, 'I'll take care of it'.

ಕೊಡು (kodu, 'give') - do it for someone else: helikodi, 'tell-give' = teach, explain; maadikodi, 'do it for me'; torisikodi, 'show me how'.

ನೋಡು (nodu, 'see') - try: tindu nodi, 'eat and see' = taste it; maadi nodi, 'try doing it'; keli nodi, 'try asking'.

ಹೋಗು (hogu, 'go') - something happens by itself, often unwanted: kaleduhogide, 'it has got lost'; mugiduhoytu, 'it got finished / used up'; haalaagihoytu, 'it got spoiled'.

guide.title: 'Without doing': the negative participle
guide.text:
The opposite of 'having done' is 'without doing': verb stem + -ಅದೆ (-ade). maadu - ಮಾಡದೆ (maadade) without doing; hogu - hogade; helu - ಹೇಳದೆ (helade) without saying; baa - barade; tinnu - tinnade; nodu - nodade.

avanu enoo helade hoda, 'he went without saying anything'; oota maadade hogabedi, 'don't go without eating'.

With iru it makes a negative command or habit: barade irabedi, 'don't fail to come'.

phrases.english: I'll go to the shop and come back.
Bring some milk. (to a friend or child)
phrases.note: 'Bring' is 'take and come'; 'take away' is tagondu hogu. Written: tegedukondu (ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡು).

phrases.english: They have gone to their home town.

phrases.note: helikodu = to teach, explain to someone.
